landmarks.name: New Lake Chalco (Lago de Tláhuac-Xico)
landmarks.summary: A new lake that formed where the ground sank, as a consequence of groundwater pumping.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground-motion number for the lake itself is still being sampled; see the Tláhuac card for the nearest measured point. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: We think the land here is still sinking, as it is in nearby Tláhuac. This is our interpretation, not a direct measurement.

drivers.human: The lake exists because of people.

landmarks.name: Tláhuac
landmarks.summary: A borough on the old Lake Chalco bed, and one of the fastest-moving places we measured.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 16 cm away from the satellite in under a year, among the fastest of the places we measured. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: The land is still sinking quickly, the same process that created the nearby lake.

drivers.human: Groundwater pumping from wells under the old lakebed.
drivers.natural: Soft lakebed clay that compresses easily.

landmarks.name: Nezahualcóyotl
landmarks.summary: A city on the eastern edge of the valley, and the fastest-moving place we measured.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 22 cm away from the satellite in under a year, the most of any place we measured. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: This is one of the fastest-sinking areas in the valley.

landmarks.name: Benito Juárez International Airport
landmarks.summary: The city's main airport, in one of the valley's sinking hotspots.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 15 cm away from the satellite in under a year. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: The airport area is sinking at a pace close to Tláhuac's.

drivers.human: Groundwater pumping and the weight of urban development.

landmarks.name: Centro Histórico
landmarks.summary: The historic heart of the city, built on the old lakebed.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 9 cm away from the satellite in under a year, slower than the eastern hotspots but still clearly moving. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: Even the historic center is sinking, though less than the east.

drivers.human: Groundwater pumping and the weight of urban development.

landmarks.name: Ángel de la Independencia
landmarks.summary: The city's famous monument, which has needed new steps as the ground around it sank.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 4 cm away from the satellite in under a year, much slower than the east. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: The west side of the city is moving less than the east.

landmarks.name: Chalco
landmarks.summary: A city at the edge of the old lake, where floodwater stayed for over a month in 2024.
landmarks.radarShows: The ground here moved about 8 cm away from the satellite in under a year. (Provisional NISAR data, Nov 2025–Oct 2026, line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills.)
landmarks.weInfer: Chalco is also sinking, though more slowly than nearby Tláhuac.

drivers.human: Residents point to unchecked growth and failing infrastructure.
drivers.natural: Low-lying ground at the edge of an ancient lake.
